utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Counsel Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I forgot to ask yesterday for the newspaper article to be admitted into evidence, the newspaper article that talks about how the witness saved the Muslim. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, D14/1. No objection? It is admitted into evidence. Good morning. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Radovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Cuic. Would you please introduce yourself?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I am Gordana Cuic, born Vidovic. I was born in Pirici on the 5th of May, 1956. I am currently living in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your education?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: It's high school. I'm a tailor, a man's tailor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you work for a company, or are you an independent contractor?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I'm an independent contractor. I have my own private store from 1973.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us if you had ever made military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not even in the period from 1991 onwards?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your clients? As a man's tailor, who were your clients? Were they only Croats, only Muslims, or did you have clients regardless of their nationality or religion?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: People came regardless of their nationality or their religion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you live in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: In Ahmici. Meaning in Pirici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you live with?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: With my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and point out on the aerial map of Ahmici, point out the place where you lived, and also could you please tell us who your neighbours were, indicate their houses, and tell the Court which neighbours were Muslims and which ones were Croats. So would you please stand up and use the pointer. So start with your house.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: This is the main Travnik-Sarajevo road. On the left is the road for Ahmici. This is my house (indicating), my mother's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who your neighbours were?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: My neighbours were -- this is the house of Zoran Kupreskic (indicating), this is the house of Mirjan Kupreskic, his parents' house (indicating). Now I'm coming back. This is the road to Ahmici. There is the house of Vlatko Kupreskic -- I'm sorry, I skipped over -- when you go on the Ahmici road, the entire right side is inhabited by Muslims, which means that on the left side are the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us some of your Muslim neighbours.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: My next-door neighbour is Smajl Pezer. That's here (indicating). The second is Sulejman Pezer. Those are my closest neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What relations did you have with your Muslim neighbours?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean, that you had good relations?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, we visited one another from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take part -- did you celebrate their religious holidays in any way?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I did take part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I was present at the ceremony, the opening ceremony for the mosque. There was a special celebration which I attended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go by yourself, or were you invited?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I was invited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who invited you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: The owner of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the owner of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Hazim Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were invited to the opening ceremony of the mosque, please tell us, did you attend the prayer inside the mosques, or were you just outside the mosque?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I attended the prayers inside the mosque, in the section where the women were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The prayer with the Muslims, women are separated from the men?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the opening ceremony, were there any music groups present, some bands?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Please sit down so that you don't have to stand any longer. So we were talking about the musical part of the opening.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was there?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: There was a band, an orchestra from Sarajevo, the so-called Ilahije and Kaside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they singing?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: They were singing their special prayers. I couldn't understand that in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in Arabic?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you started to work as an independent businesswoman, tailor, did you work alone, or did you have any employees? I'm not interested whether that person was reported as a worker or whether they worked for you.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was her name?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I had a lady, her name was Izeta Ribo. She was from Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was her nationality?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: She was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when did she work for you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: She worked from 1985 until 1989.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did she stop working with you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Her children were sick. She had twin girls, so she had to be with them every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your work, where did you work, at home or did you have rented premises?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, not at home. I had rented premises on the outskirts of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the owner of the house where these premises were?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Mahir Merdan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how long were you renting the space from him?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: From 1984 until the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mahir Merdan, what was he by nationality?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What relations did you have with him?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Very good. Very good. And when the war ended, when I started to work again, I couldn't go back to that facility again, to that space. I had been there for a long time, and I was emotionally connected with them. They were very good to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they go back to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are they now, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: As far as I know -- the owner visited me when I started to work again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, after the truce. And she said, without going into it in detail, that they are just currently living in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But she didn't say anything whether she was coming back or not?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1991, the first elections were held in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Were you involved in political activity at all, or was that something you were not interested in so you can't really give us your view of that?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't interested. I worked, I did my work, so I'm not really well informed about politics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the elections, were there any changes in the national composition of the clients in your business?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So everybody who came to you before, regardless of whether they were Muslims or Croats, they continued to be your clients? Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they were my clients, because I worked very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me now -- this will be important to explain some things later -- what were your business hours?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: My business hours, from 8.00 to 12.00, then I had a break from 12.00 to 3.00, so I would come back to work from 3.00 to 6.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So please tell us, how did you get to work? Did you use public transport?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I used public transport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you please tell me, after the first free elections did you ever see Muslims with weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. I would see them on the section of the road when I was going home, mostly around the mosque, around the mosque. Groups, small or larger groups. I really didn't pay them that much attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have weapons and uniforms, or weapons without uniforms?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So arms and weapons also, as well as civilian clothes and weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Croats with weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, I didn't have the opportunity to see them, because when I come to my house, the first Croat house is my house, when I come home from the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understood you properly, going to work and returning from work you would pass through the part that is inhabited by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So according to what you indicated on the aerial photograph, did you pass by the mosque?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when the first armed conflict broke out between Muslims and Croats in the region of the Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I think that happened on the 20th of October in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what were you doing on that day?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, it was a normal work day, so I set out for work. Across the street from my house is the house of Smajl Pezer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see something unusual in front of Smajl Pezer's house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I did see something unusual, so I came back. I was frightened and I came back. There were about 20 people who were not known to me. I couldn't tell who they were. They were Muslims and they were gathered there. Probably something was wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they look? Could you describe them? Did they have any slogans, any signs with them, or did they have something more concrete with them?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: They had weapons and uniforms, as far as I could see, and the distance is about 50 metres, so it's halfway from my mother's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe that group of Muslim soldiers that you had seen? Were they holding a position or were they sitting around smoking? What were they doing when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see the whole group. I couldn't because next to Smajl Pezer's house there is a concrete fence, and it's of uneven height. In some places, it was half a metre high. Some places it was lower; some places it was higher. I really couldn't see exactly what they were doing, but the section that I could see -- the people who I could see were in uniform. This part here (indicating), they had something. Whether there was a gun or a rifle, I don't know. They did have something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they in a group or were they dispersed?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: They were aligned. They were standing next to the fence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean, one next to the other?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, one next to the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe, when they were standing like that next to one another, how were they holding their weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I can't really -- I really can't say how they were holding their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then what did you do when you saw that group of Muslim soldiers? What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, there was shooting that started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This group that you saw was shooting or not?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see whether they were shooting or not, but just below my mother's house where I had arrived, well, of course, we were afraid, so we went to the shelter in my brother's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's your brother's name?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Rudo Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Rudo Vidovic's house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, that was the closest shelter. The house is newly built, and it's safer than in my mother's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you go there with to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: With my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just the two of you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to the shelter, then what happened?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, before we went in, I heard somebody shouting, "Don't shoot. It's Milka."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Milka is?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: That's my mother. When I went inside, when we went inside, there were five Muslims in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Five Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Three of them were my neighbours --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was asking you what they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Partially in uniform. Two of them were in partial uniform and three were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they armed or they didn't have weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: They all had weapons. They all had weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, the ones who were wearing uniforms, were they wearing full uniform or were they partly dressed in uniforms and partly in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Two of them were dressed in full uniform, from head to toe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other three?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: The other three were wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also from head to toe?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next? You heard them say, "Don't shoot. It's Milka."

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. We went inside. They moved to give my mother room to sit down. I asked them what was going on, why there was gunfire, but none of them answered my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long you stayed in the shelter with those Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, for quite a long time. I wasn't wearing a watch. I didn't know what time it was, but it was for about three or four hours that we stayed in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these three to four hours that you spent in the shelter with the Muslim soldiers, did you have any conversation?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It was so long. Of course, we had some conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the five who were there in the shelter, did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised three of my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Nevzudin Pezer, also known as Pedza. He's my next door neighbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's talk about him now. Was he wearing a uniform or civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. He had a rifle, but I don't know what kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Then there was Mujo Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A rifle?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, some kind of rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Then there was Ibrahim Karic. He's an elderly man. He was also wearing civilian clothes, and he had a rifle. From the conversation, I gathered it was a hunting rifle because he was a hunter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't recognise the fourth and the fifth man?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, I didn't, but, of course, while we were having a chat, I asked where they were from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they say?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: One of them said he was from Vrhovine and that he had arrived the previous night from the war theatre at Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the fifth man?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: The fifth man was a refugee who was staying in Ahmici, but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what part of Ahmici he was staying in?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I do. How can I explain it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we talk about Donja, Lower Ahmici --

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was in Lower Ahmici, in Donja Ahmici. I didn't know exactly where, but he told me himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Muslim soldiers, with whom you spent a few hours in the shelter on the 20th of October, 1992, make any trouble for you? Did they provoke you or mistreat you in any way?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were polite?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they were really extremely polite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time, did you smoke?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I smoked, but I ran out of cigarettes, and I asked Ibrahim Karic, since he was the eldest of them, and said I would go to my mother's house which was some 20 or 30 metres away to fetch some cigarettes and to make some coffee. So I left the shelter, and when I came back --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your mother stay?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, my mother stayed in the shelter. When I came back, none of them were there anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you spent in the shelter with them, what were they doing in the shelter?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I don't know with what intention they came to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these people leave the shelter at any moment during the shooting?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. They were in the shelter the whole time, but I tried to go out a few times, and they prevented me. They said, "No, there is gunfire." They didn't leave the shelter for a moment during the time I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they shoot?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: None of them?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, none of them fired any shots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your impression? The Muslims in the shelter, do you think they were holding a position or do you think they were hiding so as not to be wounded, killed, or can't you say?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I can't say. I really don't know why they came to the shelter. I don't know what their aim was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you couldn't gather that from their conversation?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went home and you came back, and they had gone. Did your mother perhaps tell you when they had gone and why?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, they didn't say anything. When I left the shelter, they simply went, and my mother didn't see in what direction they'd gone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They hadn't told her why they were leaving?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No, they didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that day end?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: When the gunfire stopped, we went home, of course, to our house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the Muslims in Ahmici, after this armed conflict, left Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that they left and that after a certain time they came back?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. The part where I passed through, they were all there. Either they were all there or I wasn't really paying attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this event and before the war broke out, did you see armed Muslims, Muslim soldiers, either individually or in groups?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. I would see them when they were coming back from the front, Visoko, and I don't know the names of all those places, but they would shoot. I was frightened. I didn't know why they were shooting, and I would find out later why they were shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the Muslims from your village going for some kind of training or exercise?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe that?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, it was a normal working day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what month it was, what year?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, it was approximately in mid November 1992. I have already said that I had a break at noon, so this was between 2.00 and 3.00 p.m. On the road, I met a rather large group of Muslims --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You couldn't tell us the exact number?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, I couldn't, but it was a big group. There were quite a lot of people in the group who I didn't know, and they were led by Fuad Berbic. In the group, there were quite a few Muslims whom I knew who lived in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you talked to Fuad Berbic when you met them?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. I said hello. He didn't respond. Instead, he said, "Neighbour, don't be afraid. This is only an exercise." So I waited to let them pass, and then I went on to work, as usual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the group, you said there were quite a few people you didn't know.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were there also people whom you knew?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were people I knew. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you enumerate the names of the people whom you knew and who were in that group and whom you remember now?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I could. Midhat Berbic, Hasko Berbic, Vehbija Ahmic, Fehim Ahmic, Mirsad Ahmic, Smajl Pezer, Sulejman Pezer, Osman Pezer, Nevzudin Pezer, Nedzad Dzidic, Besim Ahmic. That is as far as I can remember at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met this group of Muslims, what did the group look like? Were the members dressed in civilian clothes or in military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Some of them were in uniform. Some of them were in uniform, and most of them, the ones I didn't know, were wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they wearing any kind of insignia on their sleeve showing that they belonged to some kind of army?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I didn't notice. I didn't look at them that much because I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what your feeling was, how you felt when you heard gunfire in your village and when you heard that these were Muslim soldiers on their way back from the front and shooting? Did this have any kind of effect on you? Were you afraid?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Of course, I was afraid. I was terribly afraid of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that when you met this group of soldiers, you were frightened. Why were you frightened?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I was frightened because wherever they were gathered together in a large group, they would take the opportunity to shoot, and they had weapons. So of course I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe where you met that group of soldiers, near what houses?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: On the way out of my mother's yard, so the way I take when I'm leaving Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show this on the map?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: This is my house (indicating). I went out onto the road, and just here I met them, so approximately across the road from my mother's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. While you were living in Ahmici in these turbulent times in late 1992, were there any alarms which were false, so that people had to run and hide?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any specific event, and can you place it, tell us the time?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I remember very well. One evening, it was after 11.00 p.m., my relative, Miro Vidovic, rang us up on the telephone and said that 50 Mujahedeen had come to Barin Gaj and that I should take my mother and that we should take shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Barin Gaj, how far away from your house is it?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't say how far it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you have to walk there, how long does it take?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Maybe half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If we don't know how many kilometres it is, we know how long it takes us to walk there.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I took my mother and the cow, and we set out toward the house of Niko Sakic. My mother said, "Let's go back. For God's sake, it's late at night." So we went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And nothing happened?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, nothing happened that evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry if you've already said this, but I think you haven't: What month was this?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I think it was in November, but I couldn't tell you the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was after the first conflict?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was after the first conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you take the cow with you? This may not be very important, but it shows the way of life of the people.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, we needed milk because my brother had a baby, and we had to look after the baby, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the first conflict, you went on living in Ahmici. Some of the Muslims stayed; some of them came back. So the Muslim houses were inhabited as well. Can you tell us what the relations were between the Croats and the Muslims after the first conflict or, to put it more precisely, how did the Muslims treat you personally?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: It's true that there was a change in the way they treated me. I would pass through the Muslim part of the village four times a day, and, of course, I would always say hello to them, but 90 per cent of them refused to say hello when I said hello.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were Muslims in the village?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, just the Muslims in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did the Muslims in the town treat you, because you were working in town, in Vitez, as far as I can tell?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they would treat me normally, quite normally, as usual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were no changes among the town Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, at least I didn't notice any changes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In December 1992, did you attend some kind of gathering or party or celebration where there was a mixed Muslim-Croatian attendance?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. I attended a wedding in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose wedding?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Zoran Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he marrying?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: He was marrying Marica Sakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is his mother by nationality?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: She's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what about the guests at the wedding?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: They were mixed, of all nationalities. We all celebrated together. We sang together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any incidents between Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No, there were no incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The celebration, the wedding went well?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember where you celebrated the New Year of 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, in the hotel in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any limitations on the arrival of Muslims or the entry of Muslims into that hotel?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Not that I noticed, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this New Year celebration, was there any music?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there was music.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they play?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: They played all kinds of music for the New Year celebration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any incidents between Croats and Muslims at that party?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the wedding, Zoran Vidovic's wedding, do you remember who played?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Mirjan Kupreskic and his band were playing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zoran part of the group or is he just a dancer?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, he doesn't play any instruments, but he was there as a guest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who they associated with?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, in the band, Fahrudin Ahmic played an instrument.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he play?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: The drums.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is he by nationality?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he play there all the time?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone provoke him because he's a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have passed the New Year. Can you tell us whether anything significant happened in the period between the New Year and the 15th of April, 1993, something that would stay in your memory and something that you feel should be said here in this court?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. I think that nothing significant took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me now what you were doing on the day before the war broke out, that is, on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I had a normal work day until 6.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go home?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what happened? You came home. Around what time did you come home?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: After 6.00 p.m. I'll explain that. I did all my normal house chores, and I went to Zoran Kupreskic's house with my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay there long? Were you there with interruptions?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, with interruptions. I visited my neighbour who had just -- with Zoran, I went to visit my neighbour who had just arrived from Germany.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this neighbour's name?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Ankica Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who brought her? Do you know how she arrived?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. Well, for me it was important only that she had arrived. I don't know how she got there. I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to the house of Ivica Kupreskic -- because it's the habit in Bosnia, the custom, to have that name go by the man's name -- so was only Ivica there, and Ankica Kupreskic, or were there more people there?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yeah, there were more people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those people there all the time, or were they coming and going, some were arriving, some were leaving?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, we didn't stay there long, so there were people when we arrived, and then when I went, when I left, the same people remained. How long they stayed after that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you name the people that you remember being in the house of Ivica Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Ivica Kupreskic's grandfather, Ivo Kupreskic was there, Ljubica Kupreskic was there, Vlatko's wife, Ljubo Kupreskic, Mirjan's wife was there, Mirko Sakic was there, Miroslav Pudza, Mirjan was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mirjan who?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Mirjan Kupreskic. I think that's as much as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, so you can remember that much?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the visit, how long did you stay?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, very briefly. There were a lot of people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you were in that room where everybody was, what was the discussion about? Were they talking about that there's going to be a war tomorrow, they need to cleanse Muslims from Ahmici, or were they discussing some other topics?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, these were just casual topics. We remained in Ivica's house for a short while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, tell us what you talked about. Of course, you don't know what they were talking about when you weren't there.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So only what they were talking about.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, nothing significant. Just the usual talk was there, and we were there for only a short time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what do you understand to be just normal talk?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, about the trip. We were very glad that they had arrived. They were away for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, tell us.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I can't remember the details, exactly what we talked about. There were a lot of us. I didn't really pay attention too much to the others who were also there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left Ivica Kupreskic's house, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I went back to Zoran Kupreskic's house, where my mother was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Zoran?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, Zoran came back with me. He returned with me to his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how long you stayed in Zoran Kupreskic's house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, we stayed late, but I don't know exactly what time it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Just the usual topics. We socialised, so we always had things to talk about, all kinds of things. Except politics, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you try to remember at least some of the topics, and tell us what it was that you talked about when you were socialising.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I remember well that evening we were watching an interesting tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, there was music, mostly music, on the tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, was that a domestic tape, or was that a Western-produced tape?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yeah, it was local music.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your visit to Zoran Kupreskic's house, at any time did Zoran tell you what was going to happen the next day?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he indicate in any way that he knew that war would break out the next day?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your relationship, yours and Zoran's, were they good?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they were perfectly good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, do you think that if Zoran had known that the conflict would break out the next day, would he have told you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, if he had known, he would have told me for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would he have told you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, we were so close. We grew up together, we lived together, so why wouldn't he tell us if something like that was about to happen, and if he had known?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned home, you said that in the visit to Zoran Kupreskic's house, your mother accompanied you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your mother come back home with you, or did she go back by herself?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, she came back with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You came home, and what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, we went to bed, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now this is the first day of the war, the 16th of April. How did you wake up?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: We were woken by my cousin, our next-door neighbour, Dragan Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the time? Well, if you didn't look at the watch, approximately, or if you did look at the watch, then the exact time he woke you up.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time, but it was after 4.00 a.m. I don't know whether it was 4.30 or 5.00 a.m. It was morning. So the circumstances were such that I really can't remember exactly what time it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when he woke you up, tell us, did you look at the clock, or is this an estimate of the time?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: This is my estimate of the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did Dragan Vidovic tell you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, there were no explanations. He just said to take my mother and to go to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say which shelter? Or was there just talk about "a shelter"?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: He didn't say what shelter. I decided myself which shelter I would go to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragan Vidovic, you said he was your neighbour and that he was your cousin?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course he still is your cousin. So tell us, did he hold some kind of position, a post in Ahmici, and how did he find out that you had to go to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he didn't tell you where he got this information from?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me anything. There were no explanations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he take some particular care of you, for him to come and tell you this?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, yes. The two of us were alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Women?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, my mother and I lived alone, and, of course, he was afraid for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you needed some male protection, and he saw himself as your protector. Did I understand that right?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you understood that properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were going to the shelter, which shelter did you go to?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Jozo Vrebac's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the road to the shelter in Jozo Vrebac's house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, on the road, I met Zoran Kupreskic and his family and Mirjan Kupreskic and his family. They were driving -- they were pushing their grandmother in a cart, in a wheelbarrow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they go in the same direction as you did?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I can't remember in detail what we were talking about, but we came up and we passed by them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you caught up with them; let's be more precise.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, since they had small children, we caught up with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you caught up with them. So where did you go with your mother?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I went to Jozo Vrebac's shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody else, from the people that you knew, go to that shelter?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I want to be direct, I'm interested in Zoran, Mirjan, and their families.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, yes, I already said that. We caught up with them and we passed them. There were other people from the neighbourhood who were going towards the shelter in Jozo Vrebac's house. If I need to tell you who they are, I can remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes, please tell us who they were, if you can remember how many.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: There was Dragica Omazic, Luca Omazic, with their children. We caught up with them. I can't remember exactly who else I met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what you remember is okay. At the time you were going towards the shelter, was the shooting already in progress, or not?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, not when I was going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you determine when the firing started? And where were you at the time when it broke out?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I was already in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jozo Vrebac's house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did anybody from the family of Mirjan and Zoran Kupreskic also come to the shelter in Jozo Vrebac's house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Zoran and Mirjan's parents were there. Mirjan's wife, also, with the children, in the shelter in Jozo Vrebac's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, Zoran's family went to the house of Milutin Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find that out on that same day, that Zoran's family was in the house of Milutin Vidovic? Or did you find that out on the same (sic) day?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, the same day. I came back, because that's close, and I could see Zoran's family in the house of Milutin Vidovic. I saw them. I didn't hear about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw them?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how was it that you left the shelter in Jozo Vrebac's house and went to Milutin Vidovic's house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to see Zoran's wife, to see where she was and why didn't she come to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on that day, when you were in the shelter in Jozo Vrebac's house and you went to visit the wife of Zoran in the house of Milutin Vidovic, did you see Zoran and Mirjan, except for the time that you encountered them and they were taking their families to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them, but I couldn't tell you the time when I saw them. I couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where you saw them? Did you see them on the road, or did you see them in one shelter or the other shelter?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I saw them -- most of the time I was in the shelter of Jozo Vrebac, and that's where I would see them. That's where they would come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did they come?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: They came to see how their parents were doing, and Mirjan came to see how his family was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking, you have to explain to me why they came.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what Zoran was wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I think that he was wearing jeans and some kind of military jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mirjan?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Mirjan was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if they had weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I think that they did, but I'm not sure. As far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the kind of weapons they had? Do you understand -- do you know -- are you familiar with weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, no, I don't, I'm not familiar with weapons. I don't know what kind of weapons they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, how many times in the course of that day did you see Zoran and Mirjan, if you can't tell us the exact time?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you how many times they came because --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you couldn't?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to the shelter. So on your way to the shelter, did you see any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there several roads from your house and the Kupreskics' houses that you can reach that shelter?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understood you properly, it's not essential for everybody who takes one road from your house to the shelter to meet others who would be going in the other direction, because there are several roads?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, there are several roads, and we took the shortest one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Court earlier that during the first escape, when you had heard that Mujahedeen were coming to Barin Gaj, that you had taken your cow?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to your cow that day? You left it, as far as I can understand, at your house.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. I left the shelter maybe at around 10.00 in the morning, and I went to milk the cow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was it necessary for you to milk the cow?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, because it was time to do that. You usually do that early in the morning. I told you that we needed the milk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now you were going to milk your cow, and what did you see on the road when you were going to your house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I didn't meet anybody until I got to the house of Niko Sakic. So I didn't meet anybody until I got to the house of Niko Sakic. There I met them, and they were carrying the body of Mirjan Santic on a ladder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you meet?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I met Nikola Omazic, Dragan Vidovic, Zoran Kupreskic, and Mirjan Kupreskic. They were carrying on a ladder the body of Mirjan Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything about how it was that they were carrying the dead body of Mirjan Santic?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, they didn't, but nearby there was Mirko Sakic, and of course I was afraid, so I asked him, because I'm afraid of dead bodies, I asked him what was happening, and he told me that there was shooting, there was chaos, and I couldn't go to my house. So, of course, I returned to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the end you didn't go to milk your cow?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe how the dead body of Mirjan Santic was dressed?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I only remember he had a pale blue shawl, a scarf, around his neck, but the rest I don't remember, because I was really frightened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then what happened when you returned to the shelter? Did you go back to Jozo Vrebac's house, or Milutin Vidovic's house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, I returned immediately to Jozo Vrebac's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then what happened?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: All the people inside were upset because of the shooting. Nobody knew what was going on, and you can imagine what fear there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell us what the talk was in the shelter, where did you sleep that night, and so on.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, it was not very convenient for sleeping, so there was no sleeping. I can't remember exactly what we talked about. There were all kinds of topics, important and not so important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how did you eat in the shelter?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Food was brought to us in the course of the day while I was at the shelter, so that means until 10.00, food was brought by Zdravko Vrebac, and then in the afternoon, Ivica Kupreskic, Zoran Kupreskic, and Mirjan Kupreskic brought the food a couple of times. I can't remember exactly how many times that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we are now talking about the second day of the war, the 17th of April. On the 17th of April, did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. I started toward my home again, because I wanted to fetch the cow, and I arrived at my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I saw from my mother's house a terrible scene. The houses had been burnt down. The houses I could see from my house had all been burnt down, all of them. I don't know what happened, what had happened, but I took the cow, and I took it to the house of Ljupko Vidovic, where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is this house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: It's perhaps 200 or 300 metres away from the shelter of Jozo Vrebac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you heard anything on the 17th, or did everyone remain in the shelter, did they move?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: We all moved from the shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Because we were told that there were Muslims in a nearby stream, that they had broken through the front line and there was panic, so everyone left the shelter. And I don't know, I didn't know that evening who had gone in what direction, but Mirjan's wife and children, my mother, and I stayed in the house of Ljupko Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen? Did any events occur that were rumoured?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the wife of Mirjan or Zoran stayed with you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: It was Zoran's wife, with her children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She stayed behind?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mirjan's wife?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I didn't know where she went that evening, but I learned later that she had gone to Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom did she stay there?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I think it was with Pero Santic, if I remember well. I think it was with Pero Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about rumours that you had heard before about Mujahedeen. What did that word mean to you, "Mujahedeen"?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: To me the very word "Mujahedeen" was something terrible, something that caused horror, because rumours were rife abroad that they had come to help the Muslims with a special intention to cleanse the area of everything that was not Muslim. So the very word terrified me. My mother wasn't so upset by it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the first day of the war, that is the 16th of April, what did you hear of the wartime events? You said that you heard the onset of the gunfire at about what time?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I didn't have a watch, but I think it was about half past 5.00 or 6.00. I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did the gunfire go on that day? Was it the whole day?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, it was almost the whole day, but I don't remember whether it was more intense in the morning or in the afternoon. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell light weapons from mortars, recoilless guns?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, no. I can't tell the difference. I can only say whether it was more intense or less intense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was it very intense, or less intense?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: There were both kinds of sounds, I think, but I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you were able to assess from what direction the gunfire came?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, no, I couldn't tell from what direction it came. There were lots of houses, and I can't really -- I don't know how to judge this. I can't explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the first day of the war, was there shooting throughout the day, or were there lulls in the gunfire? Did it stop at night?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. No, I can't remember these details exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If you can't, you can't. On the 17th, the second day of the war, was there any gunfire?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, but less than the previous day. Less, so that I didn't have to run to my house to get the cow. Less. There was less gunfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the second day of the war, did you see Zoran and Mirjan?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they came to Ljupko Vidovic's house, but I can't say how many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it once, or several times?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: It was several times, but I can't tell you the number of times they came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any conversation with you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Of course, I said hello, but they probably had, that is Zoran, had private conversations with his wife. I assumed they were discussing what to do next, but I don't know, actually, what they were talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Afterwards, when the war was already going on, did you stay in Ahmici, or did you move to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: We stayed in Ljupko Vidovic's house for a certain time. I don't know how many days it was. Then my mother and I returned to our own house in Pirici, that is, in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is living in your house now?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: My mother. I live in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your mother alone now?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you go to visit your mother?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, regularly. Almost every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were talking to your fellow villagers, did they ever mention anything that might indicate intolerance toward Muslims, a desire to cleanse Ahmici of Muslims, to expel the Muslims from Ahmici, to burn their houses, and so on?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: This never happened in my presence. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was your impression, as far as you know, what were the relations between the Croatian and Muslim villagers in Ahmici, between the individuals, before the war?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: As I see it, it was perfectly good. Our neighbourly relations were perfectly good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also a dancer, or did you play a musical instrument?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, but I gave that up a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did you stop?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: In the '80s. I can't tell you the exact year. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there before Zoran, or --

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was in the group before them, and then Zoran and Mirjan came, and they continued, but I stopped because of my work and my shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you continue following the work of their company? Did you go to their performances?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the group which played musical instruments and danced, were there any Croats? Were there any Serbs there, any Muslims, any Gypsies, or was it a closed society for just one nationality?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No, all the nationalities were represented. I can even enumerate the people I know. There were Serbs, Gypsies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Cato Veljko, who is a Serb by nationality. Then I know a Gypsy, Adil, but I don't know his second name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I know his second name, but let's leave it at Adil.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Then a Muslim I know, Nedzad. I can't remember their second names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fahran?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Fahran, of course. That's understood. I forgot to mention him. Fahran is well known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was mixed?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it was mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have finished my examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Only Counsel Zelimir Par wishes to examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good day, Mrs. Cuic.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will put a few questions to you concerning Vlatko Kupreskic. In today's testimony, you indicated on the map that one of your next door neighbours was Vlatko Kupreskic, so I assume you know him and his family well?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please start talking about the 16th of April. We talked about it and you described it. Can you tell us whether, on the 16th of April, 1993, you saw Vlatko Kupreskic, when and in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him when he brought his family and his mother to Jozo Vrebac's shelter, and I asked him where his father Franjo was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about what time this was when you saw him first?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I can't tell the time exactly. I can't tell you what time it was, but they were among the last people to arrive, and the shooting had already started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can say that the shooting had started, and they were among the last to arrive?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you enumerate them?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they," who are you referring to of Vlatko Kupreskic's family?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Vlatko Kupreskic, Ljubica Kupreskic, Vlatko's children, and Vlatko's mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I interrupted you when you said you asked him something about his father. Could you continue now?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. I asked him where his father was. He said that he had stayed behind at home, that he was ill, that he couldn't walk to the shelter, and that the Muslims would not harm him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That was the first time you saw him that day?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in the shelter the whole time. Did you see him again? Did he stay in the shelter?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: During the time I was in the shelter, until about 10.00, he was there during that time in the shelter. Later, when I left the shelter and came back, after 10.00, I don't know exactly what time it was, but he wasn't in the shelter then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to milk your cow and came back, he wasn't there anymore, but you saw him there before that?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, did you see him again at all?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him in the afternoon. I can't tell you exactly what time it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: In Jozo Vrebac's shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's try to establish this. You saw him up to 10.00 and then in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know exactly when in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now I will put another question to you from another area. Is Mirko Vidovic your brother?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, Mirko Vidovic is my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where his house is in relation to yours and to Vlatko's house?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Shall I show it on the map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you can describe it.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Well, it's in the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mirko is also one of your next door neighbours?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April 1993, where was your brother Mirko?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: My brother Mirko went to Germany in March 1993. He went to visit his family who was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why his family was in Germany? Did they leave because of the war?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No. My brother's wife was in Germany for a long time because she had family there, and then he went to visit her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he left in March 1993 from Ahmici to Germany?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did he come back?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: He came back in early June 1995 to attend my wedding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was in June?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it was in June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So between March 1993 to June 1995, did Mirko come to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that on the 15th of April, 1993 he was in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Oh, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. I would now like to ask the Court whether we can go into closed session for one minute because I would like to mention a name, and that will be my last question. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Terrier:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Cuic. My name is Franck Terrier. I'm one of the members of the Office of the Prosecutor. I would like to ask you a number of questions after the testimony you have just given. I've learned that you had very good relations with Zoran Kupreskic. Will you please tell this Tribunal how these relations began and what your relations were with Mr. Zoran Kupreskic's family?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can't hear you very well. I can practically not hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now going to repeat my question, Madam. I would like for you to tell me exactly what your relations were with Zoran Kupreskic and his family, when these relations began, and what brought you together with his family.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: We, Zoran's family and my family, have known one another ever since I was born, which means that this has been inherited from our parents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the same relations with Mirjan Kupreskic and his family?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA CUIC.
utterances.text: Yes, both with Mirjan's and Zoran's parents, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
